claim: The fixed-bound Bernoulli product is an e-process for the declared composite null; the historical E_receiver_obedient score is not a one-step e-value under the fair boundary null.
command: python -c 'from fractions import Fraction as F; p0=F(1,2); q=F(3,4); vals=[p*q/p0+(1-p)*(1-q)/(1-p0) for p in (F(0),p0)]; old=F(1,2)*F(5,3)+F(1,2)*F(1); print({"filtration":"visible completed economic events through t plus predictable candidate choices", "composite_null":"P(X_t=1 | F_{t-1}) <= 1/2 for every t", "candidate_increment":"(3/2)^X_t (1/2)^(1-X_t)", "conditional_expectation_endpoints":[str(v) for v in vals], "maximum":str(max(vals)), "historical_E_receiver_obedient_expectation_after_one_fair_trial":str(old), "candidate_valid":max(vals)<=1, "historical_score_invalid":old>1})'
composite_null: All adaptive, possibly dependent laws satisfying P(X_t=1 | F_{t-1}) <= 1/2 almost surely at every indexed opportunity.
filtration: F_{t-1} contains fixed inputs, all prior legally visible completed economic events, the current opportunity definition, the already-selected candidate action and its random coin, and fixed/predictable p0_t and q_t; F_t additionally contains X_t.
method: Exact rational endpoint check supporting an algebraic affine-in-p proof; no simulation or fitting.
stopping_rule: Any filtration stopping time; Ville crossing at 1/alpha is valid. Game termination and the fixed horizon are stopping times.
